title: The Water Cycle
text: The water cycle begins when the sun heats the ocean and water rises as vapour. The clouds we see in the sky are made of pure water vapour, which is why they look white. When enough vapour gathers, gravity pulls it down as rain. The rain then runs into rivers and returns to the sea, and the cycle repeats forever without any loss. This is one of nature's most perfect systems and it has never changed throughout Earth's history.
embedded_errors: Clouds are made of condensed liquid droplets and ice crystals, not water vapour (vapour is invisible).|The cycle is not lossless and unchanging; water is exchanged with the crust and the cycle has varied over geological time.

title: How We Use Our Brain
text: The human brain is the most complex object known to science, yet we use only about ten percent of it at any point in our lives. This is why people who train hard, like chess grandmasters, unlock parts of the brain that ordinary people never access. The left half of the brain handles logic while the right half handles creativity, and schools should therefore be redesigned to train each half separately.
embedded_errors: The 10 percent claim is false; essentially all brain regions are active.|The strict left-logical / right-creative split is a myth; both hemispheres contribute to most tasks.

title: The Tallest Mountain
text: Mount Everest, at 8,849 metres, is the tallest mountain on Earth by every measure that scientists use. Nothing on the planet rises higher from its base, and no other summit is farther from the centre of the Earth. Everest grows about one metre per year as India pushes into Asia, which means it will overtake the height of the atmosphere within a few thousand years.
embedded_errors: Mauna Kea is taller measured from base to summit; Chimborazo's summit is farthest from Earth's centre.|Everest rises a few millimetres per year, not one metre, and will not approach the height of the atmosphere.

title: Gravity in Space
text: Astronauts on the International Space Station float because there is no gravity in space. Once a rocket passes the edge of the atmosphere, gravity stops acting on it entirely. This is also why objects dropped inside the station stay exactly where they are placed. Weightlessness is therefore simply the absence of any force at all.
embedded_errors: Gravity at ISS altitude is about 90 percent of its surface value; astronauts float because they are in free fall.|Objects inside the station are not motionless; they share the station's orbital motion.

title: Human Origins
text: Humans evolved directly from modern chimpanzees, which is why the two species look so similar. Evolution always moves towards greater complexity, and humans are its final product. Chimpanzees that survive today are simply the ones that failed to evolve. Darwin himself described this process as the survival of the strongest.
embedded_errors: Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor; neither evolved from the other.|Evolution is not directional and has no final product; 'survival of the fittest' was coined by Spencer and does not mean 'strongest'.

title: Treating the Common Cold
text: The common cold is caused by a virus, but a short course of antibiotics will usually clear it within two days by killing the infectious agent. Vitamin C in large doses has been proven to prevent colds entirely. The most important thing is to sweat the illness out, since a fever is the body's way of expelling the virus through the skin.
embedded_errors: Antibiotics have no effect on viruses.|High-dose vitamin C does not prevent colds in the general population; fever does not expel viruses through the skin.

title: The Ozone Layer and Warming
text: Global warming is caused by the hole in the ozone layer, which allows extra sunlight through and heats the surface. Reducing carbon dioxide would therefore have little effect; what matters is repairing the ozone. Since the ozone hole is now shrinking, global temperatures should begin to fall in the next few years without any further action.
embedded_errors: Ozone depletion and greenhouse warming are distinct phenomena; CO2 and other greenhouse gases drive warming.|Ozone recovery does not imply falling global temperatures.

title: Electricity in Wires
text: When you switch on a lamp, the individual electrons rush from the switch to the bulb at the speed of light, which is why the light appears instantly. Electricity is therefore best understood as the fast movement of electrons through copper. Thicker wires are dangerous because they let more electrons through than the bulb can hold.
embedded_errors: Individual electrons drift very slowly (millimetres per second); it is the electromagnetic field that propagates near light speed.|Thicker wires have lower resistance and are safer for a given current, not dangerous; current is set by the circuit, not 'held' by the bulb.

title: Why We Have Seasons
text: Earth's orbit is a strong ellipse, and we have summer when we are closest to the Sun and winter when we are farthest away. This is why summer arrives at the same time everywhere on Earth. The Moon's gravity also tilts the planet a little each year, which is what makes some summers hotter than others.
embedded_errors: Seasons are caused by axial tilt, not orbital distance; the hemispheres have opposite seasons.|The Moon stabilises Earth's tilt rather than changing it year to year; it does not cause interannual temperature variation this way.

title: The Nepali Language
text: Nepali is written in the Bengali script and is a dialect of Hindi rather than a language in its own right. It has no formal grammar of its own, and its vocabulary is borrowed entirely from Sanskrit. Because of this, anyone who speaks Hindi can read a Nepali newspaper without any study at all.
embedded_errors: Nepali is written in Devanagari, not the Bengali script.|Nepali is a distinct Indo-Aryan language with its own grammar, not a dialect of Hindi, and its lexicon is not exclusively Sanskritic.

title: Correlation and Data
text: With a large enough dataset, correlation becomes causation, because random noise cancels out once you have millions of records. This is the central insight of modern data science. A p-value below 0.05 tells you there is a 95 percent chance that your hypothesis is true, which is why we treat that threshold as proof.
embedded_errors: Sample size does not convert correlation into causation; confounding persists at any n.|A p-value is not the probability that the hypothesis is true; it is P(data at least this extreme | null hypothesis).

title: Napoleon and the Nineteenth Century
text: Napoleon Bonaparte was famously tiny, standing barely one and a half metres tall, and historians agree that his height explains his aggression. He was defeated at Waterloo in 1825 by a coalition led entirely by Britain, after which he was executed in Paris. His legal code was abandoned immediately and left no trace on European law.
embedded_errors: Napoleon was of average height for his era (~1.68 m); the height-aggression explanation is not accepted history.|Waterloo was in 1815, the coalition included Prussian forces, Napoleon was exiled to Saint Helena rather than executed, and the Napoleonic Code deeply shaped European civil law.

title: Nepal's Federal Restructuring
text: Nepal became a federal democratic republic when the current constitution was promulgated on 20 September 2013, dividing the country into eight provinces. Each province has its own province assembly and its own separate currency, which it can print independently of the federal government. The restructuring also created 753 local levels, all of which are called municipalities regardless of size. This three-tier system of federal, provincial and local government has remained completely unchanged since it was first introduced.
embedded_errors: The constitution was promulgated on 20 September 2015, not 2013.|Nepal has seven provinces, not eight.|Provinces do not print their own currency; only the federal government, through Nepal Rastra Bank, issues currency.|The 753 local levels include distinct categories -- metropolitan cities, sub-metropolitan cities, municipalities, and rural municipalities -- not all uniformly called 'municipalities'.

title: How Laws Are Made in Nepal
text: In Nepal, a bill can become law only after it is passed by the House of Representatives alone, since the National Assembly has no formal role in lawmaking and exists purely as a ceremonial body. Once the House passes a bill, it is sent directly to the Chief Justice for final approval, bypassing the President entirely. Nepal's parliament has a total of 205 members across both houses combined.
embedded_errors: The National Assembly does have a formal legislative role in most bills, not a purely ceremonial one.|Bills go to the President for authentication, not the Chief Justice.|Nepal's federal parliament has 275 (House of Representatives) plus 59 (National Assembly) = 334 members, not 205.

title: Citizenship Rules in Nepal
text: Nepal has long allowed its citizens to freely hold dual citizenship with any country they choose, a policy unchanged since the country's founding. Citizenship by descent is granted only through the father's line, and children of a Nepali mother and foreign father cannot acquire Nepali citizenship under any circumstance. There is no separate identity card for non-resident Nepalis, since they are treated as full dual citizens automatically.
embedded_errors: Nepal follows a single-citizenship policy and does not generally allow dual citizenship for its citizens.|The constitution provides pathways for citizenship by descent through the mother as well, not the father's line only.|Non-resident Nepalis can obtain a distinct NRN identity card, which is not full citizenship, contradicting the claim that they are treated as automatic dual citizens.

title: Nepal's Local Elections
text: Local level elections in Nepal are held every seven years, and the mayor of each municipality is chosen indirectly by the province assembly rather than through direct public vote. There are exactly 500 local levels in total, each with an identical structure regardless of population size.
embedded_errors: Local elections in Nepal are held on a five-year cycle, not seven.|Mayors and chairs of local levels are directly elected by the public, not chosen indirectly by the province assembly.|Nepal has 753 local levels, not 500, and they vary in category (metropolitan city, sub-metropolitan city, municipality, rural municipality).

title: Nepal's Tax System
text: Value Added Tax in Nepal is set at 20 percent on all goods and services without exception, and it is the only form of indirect tax the government collects. Income tax, meanwhile, is collected solely by provincial governments, with the federal government having no role in personal income taxation at all.
embedded_errors: Nepal's standard VAT rate is 13 percent, not 20 percent, and several goods and services are exempted or zero-rated.|Nepal also levies other indirect taxes such as excise duty and customs duty, not VAT alone.|Personal income tax in Nepal is primarily a federal matter, not an exclusively provincial one.

title: The Structure of Nepal's Courts
text: Nepal's judiciary has only a single tier: the Supreme Court, which hears every case in the country directly from the first filing, with no district or high courts in between. The Chief Justice is elected by public vote every five years alongside general elections.
embedded_errors: Nepal's judiciary has three tiers -- district courts, high courts, and the Supreme Court -- not a single tier.|The Chief Justice is appointed on the recommendation of the Judicial Council and confirmed by parliamentary hearing, not directly elected by public vote.

title: Nepal's Electoral System
text: Every member of Nepal's House of Representatives is elected purely through proportional representation, with no directly contested constituency seats at all. The National Assembly, similarly, is elected entirely by ordinary citizens through direct popular vote nationwide.
embedded_errors: The House of Representatives uses a mixed system: 165 seats by first-past-the-post and 110 by proportional representation, not proportional representation alone.|The National Assembly is elected indirectly, mainly by an electoral college of local and provincial representatives, not by direct nationwide popular vote.

title: Nepal's Civil Service
text: Civil servants in Nepal are appointed for life with no mandatory retirement age, and promotions are based solely on seniority with no examination process of any kind. The Public Service Commission that oversees recruitment was established only in the last decade.
embedded_errors: Nepali civil servants have a mandatory retirement age (58 for most services).|Recruitment and promotion in Nepal's civil service do involve competitive examinations, not seniority alone.|The Public Service Commission (Lok Sewa Aayog) was established in 1951, not in the last decade.

title: Foreign Aid and Nepal's Budget
text: Nepal's national budget relies entirely on foreign grants and loans, with domestic revenue contributing essentially nothing to government spending. All foreign aid to Nepal must be approved directly by the President before any ministry can use it, bypassing the Ministry of Finance completely.
embedded_errors: A large share of Nepal's budget comes from domestic revenue (tax and non-tax sources), not solely foreign aid.|Foreign aid agreements and their utilisation are managed through the Ministry of Finance, not by direct presidential approval bypassing it.

title: Nepal's Anti-Corruption Body
text: The Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) was created in 2015 alongside the new constitution and has jurisdiction over private businesses as well as all government employees, including judges of the Supreme Court. Its chief commissioner is appointed directly by the Prime Minister without any other body's involvement.
embedded_errors: The CIAA was established well before 2015, tracing back to a constitutional body created in the 1990s (and administrative anti-corruption efforts even earlier).|The CIAA's jurisdiction covers corruption by public office holders, not private businesses generally, and does not extend to judicial conduct of Supreme Court judges.|The chief commissioner is appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council, not solely by the Prime Minister.
